data.long_meaning: Aaghaa (آغا/آقا) is a Persian and Turkic title meaning 'lord, master, sir', used as a mark of respect and also as a given name. It entered Urdu as 'Agha'. As a personal name it carries the sense of a respected lord.

data.etymology: Persian/Turkic āqā, a title of respect meaning 'lord, master'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaghaa total 19, reducing to 1. Number 1 is traditionally associated with its own character. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aaghaa mean?

faq.a: Aaghaa is used as a male name.

faq.q: How is Aaghaa written in Arabic and Urdu?
faq.a: Aaghaa is written آغا in Arabic and آغا in Urdu, and आग़ा in Devanagari.

faq.q: Is Aaghaa a name or a title?
faq.a: Aaghaa (āqā/agha) is originally an honorific title meaning 'lord' or 'master'; it is also used as a given name, especially in Persian and Urdu.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aaghaa?

It entered Urdu from Persian/Turkic as 'Agha', used both as a title of respect and as a personal name.
